title: Artists and their works.
lede: Six artists and eleven of the most famous images ever made: who made what, the style each is known for, and roughly when they lived.

card.title: Artists and their works
card.desc: Leonardo to Dalí: eleven famous works, their artists, styles and centuries.

questions.ask: What style are they known for?

items.hook: Stolen from the Louvre in 1911 by a handyman who walked out with it under his smock. Two years missing made it the most famous painting on earth.
Painted on a monastery wall in Milan with an experimental technique that began flaking within his own lifetime.
A drawing, not a painting: one man fitted into a circle and a square, after the Roman architect Vitruvius, who reckoned the ideal body fits both.
Not one painting but about 250, all of the pond he dug in his own garden at Giverny.
A critic sneered at the title and called the whole group “Impressionists”. The name stuck, which must have rankled.
Painted weeks after he cut off part of his left ear. The bandage is on the right because he painted himself in a mirror.
Painted to brighten the spare room in Arles for his friend Gauguin's visit. The visit ended with the ear.
The view from his window at the asylum in Saint-Rémy, painted from memory in daylight. The swirls were his idea.
His answer to the 1937 bombing of the Basque town, painted in black, white and grey like a newspaper photograph.
Not a farmer and his wife but the artist's sister and his dentist, posed before a house with a Gothic window.
Dalí said the melting clocks came to him while looking at a Camembert going runny in the heat. The canvas is barely bigger than a sheet of A4.
